trap.segment: Vegans and strict vegetarians: 72% purchase intent but only 1.3 million adults, 2.5% of adults 18-64

items.quote: They are the largest group: 17.5M adults (34% of adults aged 18-64), with 41% purchase intent for a similar concept.
Vegans show higher intent (72%) but number only 1.3M.
Office workers (9.0M, 38%) overlap with sport practitioners, and parents have the lowest intent (22%).
France's savoury snack market was worth 2.9 billion euros in 2024, and the protein snack category 480 million euros [1].
The protein category grew 11% per year from 2021 to 2024, and plant-based products are 18% of it [1].
27% of French adults bought a protein snack in the last three months [1].
Supermarkets and hypermarkets make up 68% of protein snack sales, specialised sport and organic shops 17%, online 9%, and gyms and vending 6% [1].
A blog says high-protein food revenue grew more than five-fold between 2020 and 2024, with premium prices 20% to 100% above standard products.
Barebells | Protein bars and snacks with a sport-oriented image, strong in gyms and supermarkets [4]. Bars with 16-20 g of protein and no added sugar [5].
Chickpea products exist at Carrefour, such as chickpea crisps for kids, with about 12% of calories from protein, so not a protein positioning [10].
Protein chips sold in French sports-nutrition online shops, in 6 x 50 g boxes at 12.90 euros [11].
Lentil-based protein chips (65 g, Extra Spicy) distributed through the Ankorstore wholesale marketplace [12].

Texture was the most appreciated attribute of Proteo Crisps in Italian blind tests, while a quarter of participants found Smoked Paprika too strong, so flavour intensity matters [14]

Gyms and vending are 6% of protein snack sales and specialised sport shops are part of a 17% channel with organic shops [1].
SEG1 (vegans) has the highest intent (72%) but only 1.3M adults, about 0.9M intenders, and plant-based is only 18% of the category [1][16].
SEG3 (office workers, 9.0M, 38%) is half the size and overlaps with SEG2 [16].
SEG4 (parents, 7.1M) has the lowest intent, 22% [16].
The analysts' own arithmetic, not in any source: plant-based protein snacks at 18% of 480M euros is about 86M euros, and a 2% value share is about 9.6M euros.
A GFI Europe item on French plant-based sales (+20.5% over two years) was seen only as a headline and is not used.

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The target SEG2 (17.5M adults, 41% intent) is justified from the segment figures, and the rationale explicitly rejects vegans (1.3M, 72%) and parents (22%) on size and intent. Channels follow the market shares, and claims are filtered by the analysis. The gap is pricing: the price direction is set without competitor prices, though the plan explains why and sets a shelf-price audit first.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: The messages speak to sport practitioners (gym "Après l'effort", 15 g protein, Sea Salt and Rosemary led) and reflect the positioning of a real crisp with protein versus bar-like snacks. Channels match the strategy (supermarkets, gyms, sport and organic shops, Instagram, own online shop). The minor gap is that the online shop message and the Instagram post are not explicitly tied to sport practitioners, and vegan messaging appears only as a secondary benefit, as the strategy specifies.
